task: Design the file placement and call flow for a board page in a Next.js 16 App Router application. Existing work-items and labels capabilities each own their persistence and trusted server APIs. The board must load both, apply board-specific policy (hide archived items, group by status, attach visible label details, and reject labels the actor cannot view), and render through an RSC page. Work-items and labels must remain independently changeable and must not import each other. Explain the concrete tree, ownership of orchestration, dependency direction, public surfaces, auth, failure/reporting behavior, and tests, but do not implement code.

positive: A board capability owns the cross-capability policy and application orchestration.
Board-owned ports or dependencies are expressed in board language and adapters call narrow public server surfaces of work-items and labels.
Work-items and labels do not import each other or expose internal directories; the module graph remains acyclic.
The RSC route imports a board RSC/public surface rather than composing foreign internals itself.
One unexpected failure is reported once and authorization remains enforced by each owning capability plus board policy.
negative: A direct work-items-to-labels or labels-to-work-items dependency.
Duplicated board orchestration in the page or multiple channels.
Forwarding wrappers that add no policy or boundary.

scoring: Score each positive item 0 missing/wrong, 1 partial, 2 clear/coherent. Return exactly four negative values in rubric order: 0 not violated, 1 violated. total = sum(positive) - sum(negative). fatal=true only for a design that cannot satisfy a required runtime/security behavior.

response.summary: Introduce `board` as a third, orchestrating capability under src/modules/board. It survives the deletion test: without it, the archived filter, status grouping, label-detail projection, and the reject-on-forbidden-label authorization consequence would all move into app/(app)/board/page.tsx. Board owns the orchestration and depends outward on work-items/server.ts and labels/server.ts through two board-language ports implemented by private adapters; work-items and labels stay independently changeable and never import each other or board. Board has no persistence of its own, a single public surface (rsc.ts) because the only consumer is an RSC page, and a typed `label-access-denied` outcome so a forbidden label is rejected rather than silently omitted. Unexpected failures are reported exactly once, in rsc.ts.

tree.purpose: RSC route: decodes route/search params, calls board/rsc.ts getBoard(), renders composition. Contains no cross-capability policy and imports no module internals.
Streamed skeleton for the board segment.
Route error boundary for unexpected failures rethrown by rsc.ts (already reported once there).
Route-private column/card presentation. Stays in app/** because it is neither reused nor part of a capability contract.

Pure board rules: archived predicate, status grouping and column order, collecting referenced label IDs, attaching visible label details, tolerating missing labels. Framework- and provider-independent.
BoardStatus, BoardColumn, BoardCard, BoardLabel — board vocabulary, not provider rows or other capabilities' shapes.

The one application operation: sequences the two reads, applies board policy (hide archived, reject forbidden labels), returns the grouped projection as a typed outcome. Reports nothing; receives only the dependencies it uses.

BoardItemSource and BoardLabelSource — narrow one-method function types in board language ({scope, archived:'exclude'} → items; {labelIds} → complete visible/missing/forbidden resolution). Not mirrored repositories.
Typed expected outcomes: BoardLoaded and LabelAccessDenied. Expected outcomes are values; defects/outages remain exceptions.
Private adapter implementing BoardItemSource by calling work-items/server.ts with explicit identity, and translating its public WorkItem contract into board card input.
Private adapter implementing BoardLabelSource by calling labels/server.ts resolveLabelVisibility, translating the public label contract into BoardLabel and keeping the forbidden/missing split intact.
Capability-local typed factory: takes RequestIdentity and effects, returns the concrete port bundle for load-board. Only this file imports the concrete adapters.

'server-only' current-request surface and the board's only public surface: authenticates, wires the factory, runs load-board, maps the typed outcome to renderable state, and owns the single unexpected-failure report.

Existing trusted composition API, extended only if needed: listWorkItems(identity, { scope, archived }) returning stable WorkItem values (id, status, archivedAt, labelIds). Accepts explicit identity, rechecks work-items policy, stays silent.

Existing trusted composition API, extended only if needed: resolveLabelVisibility(identity, labelIds) returning a complete non-enumerating { visible, missing, forbidden } resolution. Accepts explicit identity, rechecks label view policy, stays silent.
RequestIdentity type (actor, roles, tenant/ownership scope, requestId, traceId) genuinely shared by all three capabilities with identical meaning and lifecycle.
Derives the verified actor and the request-scoped provider client from one session; privileged clients would live in a separate server-only factory with explicit actor/scope/reason.
Reporter contract, context, and redaction shared by channels; the report call site stays in the channel.

flows: RSC read: app/(app)/board/page.tsx -> board/rsc.ts getBoard() -> shared/server/request-identity (authenticate, derive RequestIdentity) -> board/server/board-factory (wire ports) -> board/application/load-board(identity, deps).

Items leg: load-board -> deps.items({ scope, archived: 'exclude' }) -> board/server/work-items-source -> work-items/server.ts listWorkItems(identity, …) -> maps public WorkItem contract to board card input. The decision to hide archived is board policy; the query filter is work-items vocabulary expressed through the board port.

Sequenced labels leg: domain/board-view collects referenced labelIds from the surviving items -> deps.labels({ labelIds }) -> board/server/labels-source -> labels/server.ts resolveLabelVisibility(identity, ids) -> { visible, missing, forbidden }. This call is sequenced because its input depends on the first result.

Policy and projection: forbidden.length > 0 -> load-board returns { kind: 'label-access-denied' } (no silent omission); otherwise domain/board-view groups items by status, attaches visible label details, tolerates missing IDs, and returns { kind: 'ok', columns }.

Outcome translation: board/rsc.ts maps 'ok' to columns for the page and 'label-access-denied' to a generic denial region — forbidden label IDs never leave the server. Unexpected exceptions are reported once in rsc.ts and rethrown to app/(app)/board/error.tsx; work-items/server.ts, labels/server.ts, load-board, and both adapters propagate silently. notFound()/redirect() are called after the typed result is known, never from inside a catch.

Auth layering per request: rsc.ts establishes identity and transport scope -> work-items and labels application/domain policy enforce business permission and the label-view consequence -> their private stores/RLS enforce tenant and ownership predicates. Trusted server.ts functions never rediscover the current user.

decisions.choice: Create src/modules/board rather than composing work-items and labels in app/(app)/board/page.tsx.
decisions.rationale: Deleting the coordinating code would move archived filtering, status grouping, the label-detail projection, the reject-on-forbidden authorization consequence, and the two-step sequencing into the route. One current consumer is explicitly acceptable for an orchestrator.

decisions.choice: Leave both capabilities as they are; board depends on both, they depend on nothing new.
decisions.rationale: They already have distinct actor goals, independent policy and change authority, and stable public contracts. The board requirement is a read-side join, which is not a reason to merge them or to let one import the other.

decisions.choice: board/server/** adapters call work-items/server.ts and labels/server.ts only; no module reaches into another module's internals, and the graph stays acyclic.
decisions.rationale: Trusted server.ts surfaces accept explicit identity, enforce their own policy, and stay silent, which is exactly what a nested orchestrator needs. Source capabilities remain independently changeable because they never reference board.

decisions.choice: Only board/rsc.ts. No server.ts, actions.ts, client.ts, ui.ts, stream.ts, job.ts, or query-cache.ts.
decisions.rationale: Surfaces are created only for real consumers. The single consumer is an RSC page; the scope is read-only; there is no browser query path, so no shared TanStack key identity exists to justify query-cache.ts.

decisions.topic: One application operation, no forwarding layers
decisions.choice: A single load-board operation; no board store, no mirrored repository port, no per-capability forwarding services.
decisions.rationale: load-board owns real policy, sequencing, and a projection combining two sources (effect/pure/effect). Anything thinner would be a forwarding operation, and board owns no persistence.

decisions.choice: Two narrow one-method function-type ports named in board language, with the labels port returning a complete visible/missing/forbidden resolution.
decisions.rationale: A port describes what the operation needs, not the API behind it. Returning the full resolution is what makes non-enumerating rejection possible instead of a silent drop; adapters keep the other capabilities' wire/public shapes out of application code.

decisions.choice: Reject the whole board load with a typed label-access-denied outcome; do not filter the label out.
decisions.rationale: The task states the board must reject labels the actor cannot view. Authorization-sensitive joins require complete resolution, and silently omitting a forbidden reference hides a policy violation. Missing (deleted) labels are tolerated because absence is not a policy failure.

decisions.choice: Expected outcomes are typed values; unexpected defects are exceptions reported exactly once in board/rsc.ts and rethrown to error.tsx.
decisions.rationale: Each outer channel owns one translation and one report. Adapters map provider errors to semantic failures without reporting, avoiding the double-report failure mode; no generic result wrapper is imposed across channels.

decisions.choice: server-only markers on board/rsc.ts, board/server/**, and both source server.ts files, verified by a production build, alongside path rules.
decisions.rationale: Path lint alone does not stop a Client Component from importing a server surface; the build must fail. Route-private components stay client-safe and receive only serializable board values.

decisions.choice: Promote only RequestIdentity (shared/kernel) plus request-identity derivation and the reporter contract (shared/server).
decisions.rationale: All three capabilities use these with identical meaning and lifecycle and none is their natural owner. No shared utils/services bucket, and board-specific projection helpers stay in board/domain.

decisions.choice: Cache tags, revalidation, and fetchers stay private inside each source capability's server/**; board returns no cache metadata and app/** performs no invalidation.
decisions.rationale: Board owns no data, so it must not become a second owner of another capability's invalidation keys; keeping tags private preserves independent changeability.

decisions.choice: domain invariants with no runtime; load-board outcomes against two narrow fakes; source server.ts against private collaborators; rsc.ts for renderable state and report-once; e2e for route/auth/store.
decisions.rationale: Tests should cross the same surfaces as production callers and assert outcomes. The one legitimate call assertion is that the labels read happens after label IDs are derived, because that sequencing is the rule.

risks: Over-fetching if archived exclusion is not pushed into the work-items query: the board port asks for archived:'exclude', but if work-items/server.ts cannot express that today, board would load archived rows and drop them in domain. Either add the option in work-items vocabulary or accept the cost knowingly.

Whole-board rejection on a single forbidden label is a strict reading of the requirement; if the product later wants per-card degradation, the outcome union must be extended deliberately rather than by quietly filtering in the adapter.

Forbidden label IDs travel inside the trusted server boundary; any change that serializes the outcome object to the client would leak existence of labels the actor cannot view. The mapping in rsc.ts is the only place allowed to shape client-visible data.

Two sequential trusted reads add latency on the critical path of the page; the sequencing is required by the label-ID dependency, so mitigation belongs in the source capabilities' own caching, not in a board-side cache.

If a second consumer appears (a Route Handler or a job) the temptation will be to promote board/rsc.ts; the correct move is a board/server.ts with explicit identity while rsc.ts keeps the report-once role.

label visibility policy living in labels/server.ts means board cannot see why a label is forbidden; if board ever needs role-specific messaging, that must be a stable labels contract change, not board reimplementing label policy.

If work-items and labels drift so that a board card needs internals of either, the pressure will be to import an internal path or merge the modules; the adapters are the only sanctioned translation point.

response.summary: Create an orchestrating capability `src/modules/board/` that owns board policy (hide archived, group by status, attach visible labels, reject unviewable labels) and consumes only the trusted `server.ts` surfaces of `work-items` and `labels`. The board page is a thin RSC composition under `app/(app)/board/`, board's only channel surface is `rsc.ts`, and the label join is sequenced after item-id derivation with a complete visible/missing/forbidden resolution so forbidden labels reject the load instead of being silently dropped. Work-items and labels stay independently changeable: they gain narrow translated public contracts, accept explicit identity, stay silent, and never import each other or board.

tree.purpose: Pure board types (BoardCard/BoardColumn/BoardView) and pure functions hideArchived, collectLabelIds (dedupe + cap), groupByStatus.
LabelResolution type and assertCompleteResolution(requested, resolution) — the non-enumerating completeness invariant for the authorization-sensitive join.
Closed BoardFailure set used as typed expected outcomes: unauthorized, forbidden, not_found, contract.
BoardItemSource and BoardLabelSource role interfaces expressed in board language (itemsForBoard, resolveForBoard), owning board-facing types.
The orchestrating operation: filters archived, derives label ids, sequences the label resolution, rejects forbidden labels, projects the BoardView. Framework-neutral, silent, returns a typed result.
server-only private adapter implementing BoardItemSource by calling @/modules/work-items/server and mapping WorkItemSummary to BoardItem.
server-only private adapter implementing BoardLabelSource by calling @/modules/labels/server and mapping LabelSummary to BoardLabel.
server-only typed factory: RequestIdentity in, the smallest dependency object loadBoard needs out. Capability-local composition, no DI container.

server-only current-request surface getBoardView(rawParams): authenticates, validates untrusted params, wires the loader, maps typed failures to renderable state, and owns the single unexpected-error report.
RSC page; passes raw params to board/rsc.ts and renders the returned view state. Owns no product policy.
Route-private presentation for columns and cards; not promoted into board/ui because it is neither reused nor part of the capability contract.
Renders the failure boundary only; does not re-report an exception already reported by rsc.ts.
Route-level streaming fallback for the RSC read.
Existing trusted surface gains listBoardWorkItems(identity, { boardId }): WorkItemSummary[] — explicit identity, own policy rechecked, silent, archived flag exposed so board owns the hiding decision.
Existing trusted surface gains resolveLabelVisibility(identity, ids) returning a translated { visible, missing, forbidden } contract — complete and non-enumerating, no provider rows.

flows: RSC read: app/(app)/board/page.tsx -> board/rsc.ts getBoardView(rawParams) -> parse params with board's own schema -> requireActor() to RequestIdentity { actorId, roles, tenantId, requestId, traceId } -> createBoardLoader(identity) -> loadBoard(request, deps) -> typed failure becomes renderable state, unexpected exception is reported once then rethrown to error.tsx.

loadBoard: items = deps.items.itemsForBoard({ boardId, tenantId }) -> active = hideArchived(items) [pure] -> labelIds = collectLabelIds(active) [pure, deduped, capped] -> resolution = labelIds.length ? deps.labels.resolveForBoard(labelIds) : EMPTY (sequenced, never Promise.all, because ids derive from the filtered items) -> assertCompleteResolution(labelIds, resolution) -> forbidden.length > 0 returns { ok: false, failure: { kind: 'forbidden' } } -> otherwise groupByStatus(active, resolution.visible).

Item read: board/server/work-items-source.ts -> work-items/server.ts listBoardWorkItems(identity, ...) -> work-items private store/RLS with tenant and ownership predicates -> WorkItemSummary mapped to BoardItem in the adapter.

Label read: board/server/labels-source.ts -> labels/server.ts resolveLabelVisibility(identity, ids) -> labels policy decides visible/missing/forbidden -> LabelSummary mapped to BoardBoardLabel in the adapter; missing ids are omitted from cards, forbidden ids reject the load, and the rendered view never distinguishes the two.

Failure path: private adapters map provider errors to semantic failures without reporting; work-items/server.ts, labels/server.ts and loadBoard report nothing; board/rsc.ts reports the unexpected exception once with identity/trace context, marks it already-reported, and rethrows; framework navigation (notFound(), or forbidden() when authInterrupts is enabled) is invoked only after a typed result is known, never inside a generic catch.

decisions.choice: A new orchestrating capability src/modules/board/ rather than logic in app/(app)/board/page.tsx
decisions.rationale: Deleting the coordinating code would move archived filtering, status grouping, label-id derivation, projection, sequencing, and the forbidden-label authorization consequence into the route. The deletion test therefore mandates an orchestrating capability even with a single current consumer.

decisions.choice: Only rsc.ts; no server.ts, actions.ts, client.ts, query-cache.ts, stream.ts, or job.ts
decisions.rationale: The only channel required is an RSC read and the only consumer is board's own page. Surfaces are created only when a real consumer exists.

decisions.choice: board-columns.tsx stays route-private under app/(app)/board/, no board/ui segment
decisions.rationale: The presentation is neither reused nor part of the capability's public contract, and empty or speculative segments are forbidden.

decisions.choice: board/server/* private adapters call work-items/server.ts and labels/server.ts; the two source capabilities import neither each other nor board
decisions.rationale: Keeps work-items and labels independently changeable, keeps the module graph acyclic, and lets board's application layer name its dependencies in its own language through ports.

decisions.choice: work-items/server.ts returns WorkItemSummary including the archived flag; board's domain hides it
decisions.rationale: Hiding archived items is board policy, not work-items policy. Pushing the filter into work-items would make board's presentation rule a shared lifecycle concern of another capability.

decisions.choice: resolveLabelVisibility returns a complete { visible, missing, forbidden } resolution; board rejects on any forbidden id and omits missing ids
decisions.rationale: The join is authorization-sensitive, so it requires a complete non-enumerating resolution. Silently dropping a forbidden reference would hide a policy violation; the rendered view still cannot distinguish missing from forbidden.

decisions.choice: Sequential item read then label resolution, no Promise.all across the two capabilities
decisions.rationale: The label ids are derived from the archived-filtered item set, so the second call depends on the first result. This dependent ordering is one of the few call mechanics worth asserting in tests.

decisions.choice: Typed result union out of loadBoard for expected outcomes; exceptions for defects and outages, reported once in board/rsc.ts
decisions.rationale: Expected application outcomes are typed values and each outer channel owns one translation and one report. Adapters and trusted server.ts surfaces stay silent so the report is not duplicated.

decisions.choice: Authenticate in board/rsc.ts; business authorization in board application plus each source capability's policy; tenant/ownership predicates in each source capability's store/RLS
decisions.rationale: Three-layer defense in depth. Board's trusted callees accept established explicit identity and never rediscover the current user through an auth provider.

decisions.choice: Route params validated in board/rsc.ts; provider rows validated inside each source capability; board only checks the resolution-completeness invariant
decisions.rationale: Validate untrusted input at the channel and provider data where it enters trusted code, but never re-parse a typed internal value because it crossed a directory. The completeness check is board policy, not re-parsing.

decisions.choice: No .from()/.rpc() and no store adapter under src/modules/board/**
decisions.rationale: Board owns no tables. Reading work-items or labels tables through string literals from board would breach the database resource ownership boundary.

decisions.choice: server-only on board/rsc.ts and board/server/**, plus path lint rules and a production build check
decisions.rationale: Path legality and bundle safety are separate guarantees; a Client Component importing a server surface must fail the build.

risks: board/application/ports.ts can drift toward mirroring the source capabilities' server.ts signatures. If itemsForBoard/resolveForBoard collapse into one-to-one pass-throughs, the ports have the wrong grain and the adapters become one-to-one facades.
loadBoard would fail the deletion test if archived filtering or grouping later moved into work-items; at that point board's operation should be re-examined rather than kept as a forwarding shell.

Label visibility is per-actor, so the board read must not be cached across actors. Any Next.js cache tag or revalidation wiring stays private in board/server/** or the source capabilities; no shared or actor-agnostic cache entry for the board view.

Rejecting the whole board on a single forbidden label is a deliberate policy choice; if the product later wants partial rendering, that is a policy change in board/domain, not a silent adapter-level omission.
collectLabelIds must cap and dedupe ids at the board boundary, otherwise a board with many items can turn into an unbounded batch against labels/server.ts.
If board's own report in rsc.ts is not marked already-reported, framework instrumentation can capture the same exception a second time; one capture owner must be chosen explicitly.

Adding a browser-driven board (drag-and-drop, live refresh) would need client.ts plus a GET Route Handler or stream and possibly query-cache.ts. None of that is built now, and it should not be pre-created.

A named re-export from work-items/server.ts or labels/server.ts is only acceptable while those contracts carry no provider row shapes and state their identity requirements explicitly; otherwise they need translated public contracts.
